To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IgG binding to rat intestine reaches maximum levels during second week of life and declines upon weaning.

(1) the binding of IgG to the rat intestinal MVM is maximum by day 12 of postnatal development and shows a decline upon weaning; (2) the FcRn expression is maximum during second week postnatally; (3) cortisone and thyroxine administration to suckling rats induces precocious decline in the IgG binding and receptor expression; and (4) insulin does not affect the IgG binding to the intestinal MVM or the receptor expression
the expression of IgG binding receptor on the microvillus membrane of rat intestine during post natal development is a hormone controlled process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the expression and function of FcRn in the intestine during postnatal life and the effect of hormones on the expression and function.
the study of immunoglobulin G receptor (FcRn) during postnatal development and its hormonal regulation.
the expression of the IgG receptor during the postnatal development of the rat intestine and how this process is affected by the administration of hormones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of FcRn in intestine is regulated by the endocrine system, the nature of which is not yet clear, and that it is a hormone regulated event.
the expression of the FcRn gene during postnatal development, in rat intestine is regulated by hormones.
IgG receptor expression in rat intestine during the postnatal development is regulated by cortisone and thyroxine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IgG receptor in intestine is developmentally regulated and its expression is modulated by cortisone, thyroxine and insulin.
the expression of IgG receptors in the intestinal mucosa is developmentally regulated.
the IgG binding and receptor expression is maximum during the period of suckling and is regulated by hormones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IgG receptor expression in the intestine during postnatal growth is a hormone regulated event.
the IgG binding to rat MVM reaches maximum level by day 12 of postnatal development and the expression of IgG binding sites is regulated by hormones such as cortisone and thyroxine.
FcRn is a hormone regulated protein and its expression in intestine during early postnatal life is under the influence of cortisone and thyroxine.
